title: Your own paper library
intro: A few hundred papers on trust in a small database on your laptop, with a chat page that answers from them. About 30 minutes, no new accounts.

why.title: Why not just Consensus, Scite or Zotero?

tools.name: Consensus
tools.does: AI search over 200 million papers, with cited answers.

tools.name: Scite
tools.does: How a paper was cited: supporting, contrasting or just mentioning.

tools.name: Zotero
tools.does: Free reference manager. Citations into Word and Google Docs.

reasons.title: Your sources
reasons.body: One topic, from sources you pick, including working papers or your own PDFs.

reasons.title: Your columns
reasons.body: Method, sample, country, your own codes. Claude reads each abstract and fills them in.

reasons.title: Your questions
reasons.body: Which papers use field experiments outside the US? A count per year, as a chart.

reasons.title: Yours to keep
reasons.body: No subscription, nothing uploaded, and you can see how it searched.

why.limits: It holds hundreds of papers, not millions. Use them together: find with Consensus, check with Scite, cite with Zotero. Claude can export your library as BibTeX for Zotero.

steps.title: Start a new project
steps.body: Code tab, new project, then pick or make a folder.

steps.title: Say what you want
steps.body: Swap "trust" for your own topic if you like.
steps.say: Hi Claude. I'm a researcher and I want my own little library of papers about trust: who people trust, why, and what breaks it. Grab a few hundred from arXiv and from OpenAlex (title, authors, year, abstract, link) and keep them in a small database in this folder so I can search it. Keep it simple, I'm not technical, you decide how. When it's done, show me how to ask it a question.

steps.title: Let it work
steps.body: Mine ended by suggesting Python scripts. Skip those.

steps.title: Ask for a page instead
steps.say: Now make me a little webpage that's a chatbot that I can use instead of your weird scripts.

steps.title: Keep it on your laptop
steps.body: If it offers a Claude artifact, a page on Claude's site, say no.

steps.title: Ask for a page, not an app
steps.body: If it wants to set up a helper app.
steps.say: Make me a web page instead, still hosted locally.

steps.title: Open your library
steps.body: Double-click the launcher it made (mine is called Open Trust Shelf). Leave the small Terminal window open while you chat.
steps.trap: If macOS blocks it: right-click, Open, then Open again.

steps.title: Ask it something
steps.body: It answers from your papers only, names the paper behind each claim and links to it. It has read the abstracts, not the full papers.

steps.title: Ask for more
steps.say: Make it a full chat bot.

next.title: Tomorrow
next.body: Double-click Open Trust Shelf. In Claude, rename and pin the project so you find it.
